selection: Common retail categories with weaker category-specific coverage in this research corpus; not a measured sales ranking.

entries.title: Serial numbers matter in a major battery recall
entries.finding: Recall 25-466 (2025-09-18) names Anker A1647/A1652/A1257/A1681/A1689; CPSC directs consumers to verify serial numbers. Reported fire/burn incidents are product-specific.
entries.application: Match model first, then official serial scope; do not collect/upload serial numbers or identity passively. Preserve exact model/serial distinction.
entries.limits: No all-Anker warning; no current listing inspected or serial lookup submitted.

entries.title: Vendor serial-check guidance is not an open lookup API
entries.finding: Vendor lists the same five models and a serial/proof-of-purchase recall form; warns about confusable characters.
entries.application: Offer explicit official lookup; retain raw OCR and ask user to verify confusable characters.
entries.limits: No undocumented API or automatic claim submission; never silently correct a serial.

entries.title: USB certification is capability-specific

sources.depth: opened; product-search description read, no lookup submitted

entries.finding: USB-IF public search covers products certified for its logo, maintained by member firms; default filter shows only two years. Older records require date filtering.
entries.application: Preserve lookup filter and age before declaring missing certification; a found record supports its own tested scope.
entries.limits: No exact product lookup made. Absence is unresolved, not counterfeit; USB compliance is not general electrical/fire certification.

entries.title: Power rating and data speed are separate claims
entries.finding: USB-IF cable program distinguishes purposes/capabilities; its current USB-C-to-C certification label guidance lists 60W or 240W power icons.
entries.application: Extract power/data features independently; retain label-claim versus certification-verified states.
entries.limits: Do not call a legacy 100W cable unsafe based on a newer logo scheme; no physical/e-marker/protocol test performed.

entries.title: FDA registration certificates are a misleading-claim gap
entries.finding: FDA's 2026-09-09 update says it does not issue cosmetic registration/listing verification certificates. Registration/listing does not establish FDA approval; some small businesses are exempt.
entries.application: A claim of FDA-issued cosmetic registration certificate deserves source/issuer checking. Compare exact claim to FDA statement and preserve quote/locator.
entries.limits: A third-party registration service is not automatically fraud; missing listing is not proof of illegality. Drug/medical claims require separate classification.

entries.title: A tested-product list supplies precise safety leads across platforms
entries.finding: FDA's product-specific laboratory table includes Collagen Plus Vit-E Night Cream sold on Etsy (2022: mercury 3,670ppm; hydroquinone 2.0%) and Deluxe Silken Bleaching Cream sold on eBay (2026: mercury 19,027ppm; reported Jamaica origin). Those sampled products are not a platform prevalence estimate.

products.name: Collagen Plus - Vit E Cream, Night Cream

entries.application: Match exact name/package and sample year; source hazard to tested product; keep listing-removal, warning and recall states separate.
entries.limits: Current listings and same-name batches unverified; no new product laboratory testing. Region is table metadata, not inferred.

entries.title: Serial-restricted licensed-brand appliance recall
entries.finding: Recall expansion 26-199 (2026-01-15) names red EFMIS121 minifridges, serials A2001–A2310, Target sales. Manufacturer ShangYu North Electron Manufacture; importer Curtis International of Canada; origin China. CPSC reports at least six fires with property damage.

identifiers.manufacturer: ShangYu North Electron Manufacture Co. Ltd.

entries.application: Separate brand license/marketing identity, manufacturer and importer; preserve bounded serial scope and expansion lineage.
entries.limits: Expansion text says July 2024, but its linked original 25-395 is dated July 24, 2025. Preserve source conflict. Serial scope and EFMIS129 suffix exclusions govern; do not warn on every Frigidaire model.

entries.title: Historical seller changes can alter recall remedy
entries.finding: Recall 25-311 (2025-06-05) covers BowFlex 552/1090 and listed serial ranges. Notice distinguishes units sold by pre-bankruptcy BowFlex/Nautilus from Johnson Health Tech Trading and different remedies. Origin China.

identifiers.exampleScope: 1090; illustrative one range, not complete list

entries.application: Use exact serial-family ranges and purchase period; importing brand-wide current safety or remedy status would be wrong.
entries.limits: Weights/capacity cannot be verified from listing photos. No physical retention/strength test, exhaustive serial transcription or current notice refresh beyond this retrieval.

entries.title: Small coin-battery lights can create household hazards
entries.finding: 26-403 (2026-04-09): Happiness Light 24-pack, two CR2032 cells per round light, accessible batteries/missing warnings. Retailer J U Kai Technology; China origin.
entries.application: Classify components as well as intended decor use. Store exact package/count/design scope.
entries.limits: No general battery-accessibility judgment from a photo. Factory unknown; no unique SKU obtained.

entries.title: USB low-voltage products can still have fire hazards
entries.finding: 25-204 (2025-04-03): Room2Room bear-light USB switch overheating/melting, with burns/property damage. Distributor 1616 Holdings; retailer Five Below; China origin.

identifiers.identifierCaution: Source labels 13-digit value UPC; preserve raw rather than changing its type/value automatically.

entries.application: Match exact model/packaging and hazard component; avoid a rule that all USB-powered products are safe.
entries.limits: No all-Five Below or all-LED warning; performance/brightness/flicker untested.

entries.title: Packaging identifiers can outperform title aliases
entries.finding: 24-366 (2024-09-19) names Newmemo 36-ring sets, pink heart case, FNSKU X0034COQMP; importer Memovan Technology Industrial dba Newmemo. Lead/cadmium violations; China origin.
entries.application: Keep FNSKU, ASIN, seller ID and GTIN as different identifier types. Product matching must retain 36-ring/case scope.
entries.limits: No chemical-composition inference from silver-colored appearance. Historical seller ID does not prove present identity.

entries.title: Set descriptions and retailer identity matter without a SKU
entries.finding: 25-082 (2025-01-02) names three Yaomiao sets, retailer Wuhannuoyunxindianzikejiyouxiangongsi dba LordRoads, lavender packaging; lead/cadmium violations, China origin.

identifiers.packagePhrase: A Special Gift for the Charming You

entries.application: Combine package phrase, set composition, source images and retailer history as identity candidates.
entries.limits: Phrase alone is nonunique; no all-Yaomiao product warning, no chemical tests executed.

entries.title: USCG equipment lookup has explicit coverage exceptions
entries.finding: CGMIX lists approved/certified vessel/boat equipment, with some European Notified Body MRA approvals located elsewhere.
entries.application: Offer official approval lookup; preserve jurisdiction and exceptions before evaluating a missing result.
entries.limits: Database/API access, exact product searches and other-jurisdiction coverage untested. Unknown is not fake approval.

entries.title: Approval expiry does not always invalidate an existing item
entries.finding: CGMIX distinguishes Approved, Former-May Use, Former-May Not Use and Expired. Its Expired definition says items manufactured before expiration are considered approved.
entries.application: Store approval status and manufacture date together; avoid a simplistic expired=unsafe rule.
entries.limits: Current serviceability, intended use, size/fit and physical buoyancy untested; no product approved by this research.

entries.title: UL country codes describe standards geography, not origin
entries.finding: UL says enhanced-mark country codes identify standards geography. File/unique IDs can be checked in Product iQ; Listed/Classified/enhanced variants have legitimate meanings.
entries.application: Record label claim and exact lookup scope; do not treat a US mark as Made in USA or a nonpreferred mark variant as forged.
entries.limits: Logo is not self-authenticating; component recognition and end-product scope still need verification; no exact product lookup made.

entries.title: UL Product iQ is an account-based research option
entries.finding: UL describes a complimentary Product iQ account for manufacturer certification/category records.
entries.application: Explicit user research action; confirm access/API terms before any engineering integration.
entries.limits: No account created, login, requests or certificate authentication performed. No keyless bulk API assumed.

entries.title: ETL Listed and ETL Verified scopes differ
entries.finding: Intertek directories distinguish ETL Listed product safety scope from other verification directories, including cabling and specific modules.
entries.application: Select correct directory and compare complete model/category; keep multiple-listing brands and basic listee roles distinct.
entries.limits: No automated endpoint/CORS/quota/redistribution license or exact certificate tested; a directory miss is unresolved.

entries.title: Targeted inspection results include both failures and no-action samples

sources.depth: opened; sampling method and selected result rows read

entries.finding: Health Canada's 2024–25 project tested 38 imported children's-jewelry products after market survey/XRF screening, reporting three recalls, two alerts and 33 no-corrective-action instances. Several China-origin rows report no compliance issue detected.
entries.application: Use exact adverse product rows; retain jurisdiction/method/sampling selection. XRF screening and confirmatory laboratory testing are distinct.
entries.limits: This is targeted selection, not population failure rate or proof all no-action products are safe forever. Country alone cannot reproduce the observed product distinctions.

entries.title: Small XRF study is a physical-test lead

sources.depth: metadata and abstract opening read; full paper not reviewed

entries.finding: 2023 DOI 10.1016/j.jhazmat.2023.132167 describes pXRF analysis of eight low-cost adult jewelry samples from Chinese e-commerce platforms.
entries.application: Physical-assay evidence design lead; source sample/package identity must connect a tested item to a retail item.
entries.limits: Tiny selected sample; platforms/factory identities and current batches not independently verified. Browser images cannot measure metal content or migration.

entries.title: Recent publication uses old targeted surveillance samples

sources.depth: abstract/metadata read; follow-up methods retrieval failed

entries.finding: Published 2026-08-15; paper describes 197 products collected during 2009–2022 NYC store investigations, mercury testing and an associated NYC Open Data source. Ingredients alone can omit measured mercury.
entries.application: Do not confuse publication date with current-product sample date. Ingredient parsing is claim analysis, not chemical clearance.
entries.limits: Targeted store/community selection; not present marketplace prevalence. Percentages/denominator details not reproduced because deeper methods retrieval failed.

entries.title: Online cosmetics assay study deserves deeper method review

sources.depth: primary abstract search excerpt; direct opening empty

entries.finding: 2025 study 'Mercury in online skin-lightening cosmetics' reports XRF testing of 134 online-purchased products from seven Asian countries.
entries.application: Follow up sampled names, selection process, laboratory confirmation and product provenance before proposing category predictors.
entries.limits: Full abstract/methods not obtained; no numerical regional failure coefficient adopted, no paper replication.

entries.title: Official linked notices can contain conflicting dates and model exclusions
entries.finding: Original recall 25-395 is dated 2025-07-24. It lists EFMIS129/137/149/175 and serial boundaries, with EFMIS129-B/C excluded. Expansion 26-199 incorrectly or inconsistently refers to July 2024; seek agency clarification rather than invent chronology.
entries.application: Store original and expansion as one lineage with source-specific dates, plus explicit exclusion predicates. Source date conflict remains a flag in the research record.
entries.limits: No agency clarification sought, remedy performed or current retail unit matched. Source notices remain primary evidence of their own stated scope.
